## D50 first generation-result block implemented locally; final qualification pending — 2026-11-05

The investigator explicitly approves the reviewed contract (`ce32baaa65cdce9a6474f95bac3a65ec5425fd3601bbdeb8f6e8983f4f4ed70b`), now D50. A separate local `peptidemt-generation-results` worktree starts from preserved dev7 commit `a77baff9de97e8ab4ae101b9b0c79122dea22ce3`; the new source candidate is **0.0.0.dev8**, uncommitted. The clean dev7 worktree and accepted resources are untouched.

**Delivered owner code**
- Detached descriptive `generation_profile`, sharing descriptor call parameters with actual delegation, including the moment constructor scale. Known selected expectations, custom/unknown settings and unused providers remain explicit; no preparation/calculation.
- `save_generation_result` / `load_generation_result` and `GenerationResult`: five native arrays, original zeros, strings/duplicates/return permutation, existing descriptor values and explicit original provenance/unknowns. Exporter identity remains separate.
- Bounded uncompressed NPZ/JSON domain format, no pickle, typed/cross-field/header checks, duplicate rejection and no-overwrite writes. NumPy owns array encoding; no generic persistence/framework copy.
- One light owner vocabulary and lazy public imports. Existing inference classes/other functions retain their ASTs; five earlier runtime files remain byte-identical. Old exports remain mapped and a final explicit compatibility regression is included.
- Explicit optional Recorda references and detached Ackredit readers/renderers. Callers own sessions/resolution; no automatic registration, credit, model replay or PeptideMT dependency.

**Evidence is intentionally split by source identity**
Initial source checks: 46 pass /one failure caused by a harness blocker masking genuine SDK absence. The diagnosed single-selector retry passes; the original failed artifact and successful checks are retained. Five actual editable Recorda/Ackredit checks pass with no Torch import or new credit. All have zero neural/learned/PCA calls. Published Pytest Receptor 1.2.2 artifacts are complete.

After those precursor checks, profile metadata/regressions were refined. The **final 52-test source selection and exact installed-candidate qualification remain pending**; earlier passes are not relabelled as that later source. Current lint/format/compile checks pass.

The build is refused before starting once. After host recovery, the next build is interrupted by the 8 GiB available-host RAM guard at ~105 MiB aggregate RSS, not by an observed backend error. No wheel/sdist is produced or qualified. Its buffered native output had not been persisted; no exception is invented. A resumed driver now streams logs, uses fresh outputs and waits for conservative headroom. D49 already authorizes bounded continuation when the shared host recovers; no new per-run human approval is needed.

Maintained outcome: `devguide/hydramp_generation_result_implementation.md`; receipt `devguide/evidence/hydramp_generation_result_implementation.json`, SHA-256 `0df9543c431dbf3a79d605c3fd34c3e03fe68eb1b7ea561635aee0510d8b283b`. Final local managed-source manifest SHA-256 `e25932cb7e23869956401b9cdb4ee295b345534996666b250e41f5cd1d713808`; complete 19-path review patch retained locally. New owner usage/instructions and consumer decision/navigation records are updated.

#4/#2 / uibcdf/peptidemt#32 stay open. No final candidate/scientific acceptance, real descriptor/model execution, neural evaluation, GPU, live attribution, analogue/encoder archive, feedback/family/target expansion, commit/push, package publication or author contact occurs. Useful owned source/evidence is retained for the remaining qualification, review 2026-11-19.

## Current D50 implementation checkpoint — 2026-11-05

The investigator approves the first generation-result/profile contract. Private dev8 source is implemented on isolated local `peptidemt-generation-results`, preserving dev7 and accepted resources. Initial source checks pass across the recorded harness fix; five actual SDK controls pass. Later refinements still need final source and exact installed qualification.

Shared-host RAM guards refuse/interrupt the build; no candidate artifact or final qualification is claimed. Source/evidence and bounded continuation drivers are preserved. D49 authorizes resumption when host headroom recovers, without another routine permission round. Details: https://github.com/uibcdf/hydramp/issues/4#issuecomment-6674244559. No neural/learned calls, new scientific acceptance, commit/push, release or author contact.

## Previous result-contract review checkpoint — 2026-11-05

A concrete independent generation save/read proposal is ready for investigator review: https://github.com/uibcdf/hydramp/issues/4#issuecomment-6673257407. It preserves the existing native arrays, token/string distinctions, occurrence mapping, scores/descriptor values and provenance unknowns, with original producer and later exporter identities kept separate. One NumPy archive is recommended; optional caller-owned Recorda references and detached Ackredit data retain their existing owners. Related descriptive profile work remains in #2.

The controlled NumPy storage primitive passes on synthetic arrays without Torch/models. The combined provider mechanism probe never starts because of the shared-host resource guard; no integration pass is claimed. The eager package/Torch import is a concrete implementation prerequisite. This is a proposal under the existing readiness agreement, not approval or implementation of a schema/API, a new scientific acceptance or execution. Current source commit remains `a77baff9de97e8ab4ae101b9b0c79122dea22ce3`; runtime, locks and accepted resources are unchanged.

## Previous installation checkpoint — 2026-11-05

The unchanged private dev7 wheel installs with seventeen freshly downloaded, hash-verified public base/test dependency wheels in a new Linux x86_64 / CPython 3.14.7 environment. Native dependency checking passes for eighteen distributions; sixteen exports and seventeen guarded installed codec tests pass. No retained third-party payloads, learned reads or neural evaluations are used. Source remains local commit `a77baff9de97e8ab4ae101b9b0c79122dea22ce3`; its worktree is clean.

Exact scope, artifacts, limits and evidence: https://github.com/uibcdf/hydramp/issues/4#issuecomment-6672939016. This qualifies the exact public locked dependency route with a private own wheel, not public HydrAMP distribution, a clean public build toolchain, optional modlAMP or other platforms. The next product task is a concrete independent result/provenance contract review, preserving Recorda/Ackredit ownership; no new schema/API or scientific acceptance is inferred.

## Previous source/package baseline checkpoint — 2026-11-05

The investigator-authorized local `peptidemt-product-baseline` branch contains commit **`a77baff9de97e8ab4ae101b9b0c79122dea22ce3`**, exactly matching reviewed tree `2476a08a50d32779db2f43683928450e62b66f91`. Its worktree is clean and all other branch references are preserved. This commit has not been pushed. Private dev7 consolidates the existing runtime/tests/documentation/lock and packaging presentation; all nine dev6 runtime modules and original reference remain unchanged.

Directory/source-archive builds produce byte-identical wheels; a fresh installed codec check passes seventeen tests with zero neural evaluations or learned-asset reads. Native dependency checking passes. This uses faithful retained local dependency payloads, not a clean public dependency-install route or all-platform qualification. Initial engineering failures are diagnosed and retained.

Exact artifacts, scope and evidence: https://github.com/uibcdf/hydramp/issues/4#issuecomment-6672423144. The single local commit succeeds with native exit 0; prior preparation receipts remain unchanged. Git identity alone changes no package payloads, so the successful build/installed checks are reused. No push, release, new scientific acceptance or author contact follows. Independent result/workflow design and public distribution prerequisites remain open.

## Previous product-review checkpoint — 2026-11-05

Current local dev6 has nine matching source/wheel/installed modules and sixteen public exports. Encoder, analogue and codec capabilities now have separate evidence; exact dev3/D41 and dev5/D44 acceptance remain distinct. Current documentation/navigation is updated in the owner redesign worktree. No runtime code or artifact changes.

The core is an independent expert Python library in its pinned local CPU profile. Source is still uncommitted. Next: one coherent reproducible source/package baseline, build presentation/dependency-route qualification, then a reviewed independent result/workflow contract. CLI remains optional. No new acceptance, calls, training, release or contact follows.

Full current review and source/evidence identities: https://github.com/uibcdf/hydramp/issues/4#issuecomment-6671622876

## Original review commission and initial resource record (preserved)

## Purpose

Give the modern fork a systematic review as an independently usable scientific tool, rather than relying on its PeptideMT integration as proof of product readiness. Preserve the original reference and credit; this issue does not select a new public name or promise a release.

## Review scope and completion criteria

- Map supported and unsupported scientific operations, native AMP/MIC meanings, original token/string distinctions, descriptor definitions, unknown chemistry and failure behavior. Scope the modern inference port separately from unqualified training/analogue routes.
- Review standalone API/CLI usability, explicit configuration/seeds, occurrence identity, structured results, provenance and truthful diagnostics without requiring PeptideMT. Reuse existing owner tests; identify meaningful missing regressions rather than mechanically duplicating them.
- Assess reproducible CPU installation, actual dependency closure/origins, Python/dependency claims, startup/resource controls, offline operation and checkpoint/PCA acquisition. Exact local Python 3.14 execution is not all-platform support or a qualified public installer.
- Audit method/software attribution, original notices, versioning and data/model use boundaries; retain the unresolved starter-versus-original-Drive byte identity and broader redistribution/output-use questions.
- Prepare user documentation, a retained-data example, limitations/model card and a prioritized product backlog. Record observed defects in their owning issues. Machine-readable profile metadata already belongs to #2.
- Finish with an evidence-backed readiness assessment and explicit remaining blockers; packaging/release implementation and publication remain separately authorized actions.

Interest from original authors is a separate collaboration question; useful standalone modernization does not depend on creating a new algorithm.

Consumer tracking: https://github.com/uibcdf/peptidemt/issues/32
Accepted current resource: experimental AMP generation under PeptideMT D41; provider `hydramp-torch==0.0.0.dev3`, wheel SHA-256 `81761e0d48d92f0956e0afc28b3b4154f16032de53c666fd2cfbb53606102ed7`. Evidence and preserved limits: https://github.com/uibcdf/peptidemt/issues/8#issuecomment-6618984173.

This is investigator-requested future work to retain and review, not authorization for a new experiment, training, GPU, package/model release or external publication. Current model-call budgets are exhausted. Preserve the original reference, exact bundles, declared chemistry and all existing FAIL diagnostics.

## Current D50 profile checkpoint — 2026-11-05

The investigator approves the first profile/result block. A detached owner profile and shared descriptor-delegation parameters are implemented in the isolated private dev8 source, with explicit unused/unknown/declared settings and no backend preparation or calculation. Final source/installed qualification remains pending after shared-host memory guards interrupt the build; this issue is not resolved merely by source delivery.

Details: https://github.com/uibcdf/hydramp/issues/2#issuecomment-6674259622; product owner #4, consumer uibcdf/peptidemt#32. Preserve accepted resources, native definitions and all earlier proposal evidence below.

## Original proposal (preserved)

PeptideMT needs a provider-owned, machine-readable description of the selected HydrAMP generation/descriptor profile so result provenance can identify its definitions without maintaining a second editable parameter table in the consumer.

Consumer: https://github.com/uibcdf/peptidemt/issues/8
This is a separate nonblocking metadata-capability proposal from numerical-drift investigation #1.

Source inspected: the local, unpublished native PyTorch port, `hydramp-torch==0.0.0.dev3`, wheel SHA-256 `81761e0d48d92f0956e0afc28b3b4154f16032de53c666fd2cfbb53606102ed7`. Its `hydramp_torch/properties.py` SHA-256 is `c47bd6f8224b996b6d221caf2de151d3d6aae1360faf4a3ec56fdd8b09abe758`. This is artifact/source evidence, not a claim that the port is committed or publicly distributed.

Observed gap: `Modlamp433Properties` exposes `expected_version` and `pi_amide`, but other selected parameters live in method bodies: Eisenberg scale, moment window 1000/angle 100/modality=max, charge pH 7/amide=True, and the selected pI amide=False. The generation branch also defines unfiltered AMP mode, one attempt, original-zero-token scoring, returned AMP order and raw AMP/MIC meanings. There is no complete supported data-only profile record tying those meanings to the implementation. The earlier consumer qualification helper described these values itself; extending that pattern to the public adapter would duplicate provider knowledge.

Proposed capability, for owner review: publish a versioned pure-data record or public metadata operation owned by HydrAMP that describes the selected implementation, supported native route, descriptor parameters/defaults, native score meanings and relevant source/version identity. Reading it should require no checkpoint/PCA loading or descriptor/model evaluation; a packaged data resource is one possible delivery, with the implementation choice left to the provider. Clearly distinguish descriptive method defaults from evidence of a peptide's actual chemistry or scientific acceptance.

Suggested acceptance evidence:
- values correspond to the actual delegated descriptor/generation calls;
- callers cannot accidentally mutate a shared profile;
- resource/operation works without real model/PCA assets;
- unsupported or different profiles are explicit;
- preserve native calculations, scores, chemistry assumptions and existing qualification evidence.

Current consumer interim behavior: retain exact installed-provider Python hashes, implementation/version/descriptor class identity and source references; user documentation explains the selected definitions. Do not introduce another computational implementation or pretend the metadata is unavailable scientific evidence. When the provider record is delivered and its exact candidate is qualified, PeptideMT can consume it and remove any interim consumer-authored profile description.

This proposal does **not** request changing scientific definitions, precision, weights or descriptors, executing new models, publishing a package, or silently adopting a new candidate. The current dev3 bundle and proposed single installed-adapter qualification remain unchanged.
